summary.text: 百 means “one hundred” and can also mean “many,” “all,” or “various.” Accounts of its early form differ: one proposes a marked 白-like base, another a combined 一+白 spelling, and another says 白 first wrote the numeral before a distinct 百 graph was formed.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. One analysis treats 百 as an indicative graph, with a mark above a 白-like base indicating one hundred. Another reads a combined 一-plus-白 spelling and proposes that 白 was borrowed for the numeral because the words sounded alike or similar; it suggests the spelling later reduced to 百. A separate account calls 百 a “special phonetic” graph: 白 first wrote the numeral and supplied sound, and a dedicated 百 was later differentiated. That account also reads the Shang form as 白 with an added indicator, then describes lower 自 as a later corruption or change of 白. These proposals do not establish whether they describe different forms or stages.

components.text: The top mark is read either as an indicator of one hundred or as 一, “one,” in a combined 一-plus-白 spelling; these are competing analyses.

In the combined-spelling analysis, 白 supplies a sound cue. A separate account proposes that 白 first wrote the numeral as a whole graph and also supplied sound in the later 百; it describes a later lower 自 as a change of 白. These claims do not settle the earliest lower form’s identity.

sound.text: The reconstructed rhymes are similar, but 百 has a voiceless initial and 白 a voiced one. This supports a plausible sound association without proving the component analysis.

history.text: The oracle-style redraw shows a horizontal stroke above an angular enclosure with crossing interior strokes. The transmitted Shuowen seal-script redraw has a broad top above a rounded enclosure with crossing strokes; these descriptions do not establish a sequence of form development.

The received Shuowen text parses 百 as 一 plus 𪞶 and says its old form followed 自. Duan Yucai’s later annotation instead identifies the lower element as 白. These differing lexicographic readings do not settle the earliest structure.

One account proposes that a combined 一百 spelling later became 百, possibly through omission of 一 in speech. A separate account calls 百 a “special phonetic” graph: 白 first wrote the numeral and supplied sound, before a dedicated 百 was differentiated. It reads the Shang form as 白 with an added indicator and describes a later lower 自 as a corruption or change of 白. These are distinct proposals; neither the reduction nor the proposed graphic change is established, and their relation to the marked-base analysis remains unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The earliest structure remains unsettled: the top stroke may be a marker above a 白-like base or 一 in a combined spelling. The Shuowen tradition also preserves differing readings of the lower element.
The reconstructed sound comparison makes 白 a plausible proposed phonetic element, but does not prove that role or directly record the earliest pronunciation.

senses.text: 百 denotes the numeral one hundred in present-day Mandarin. Specialist accounts also report oracle-bone numerical examples and cite a Western Zhou bronze example; the cited artifact contexts have not been checked against the objects.

senses.text: 百 is also recorded with the sense “many.” A cited bronze-context example is interpreted as a possible extension from the numeral, but does not prove that development. When this sense arose remains unresolved.

senses.text: 百 is recorded with an inclusive sense, including in a cited Book of Odes example. Its chronological and semantic relation to the numeral and abundance senses is unresolved.

limitations.text: The evidence records these meanings but does not establish a continuous chronology or semantic pathway connecting them, so no developments are assigned.

relationships.text: One analysis reads 百 as 一 plus 白 and assigns 白 a sound role. Another also proposes that 白 supplied sound, while leaving the lower form’s graphic identity uncertain. The reconstructed forms of 白 and 百 have similar rhymes but differ in initial voicing, making the sound relationship plausible without settling the early graph’s analysis.
